decisions.evidence: R4 maker: paste address + 'Get details'; R5 maker: 'Save bookmark' returns to library as a card. R4/R5 client: 'After I paste the address and select Get details... I can edit both' / 'the link is sitting there as a card'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Save-by-url flow presented and confirmed; conforms to reference save behaviour.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker: 'the editable title and page description are the outcome you expect'. R4 client: 'it shows me a title and a page description that are already filled in, and I can edit both'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Auto-collection of title/description and pre-save editability conform to REF-BM-02 (title/description) and REF-BM-03 (edit before saving).

decisions.evidence: Across R4 ('title and page description'), R5 (card shows 'title, description, website') and R7 the maker consistently enumerates only title/description as collected; favicon and preview image never presented as collected or displayed. Client never raises favicon/preview in any round.
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-02 requires auto-collecting favicon and preview image (and REF-BM-07 favicon display); the presented auto-collect decision omits both. Established from the maker's explicit repeated field enumeration; passed without the client expressing the difference.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker: Version A click card vs Version B button, both 'open the original site in a new browser tab'. R6 client: 'clicking the card itself takes me straight to the site'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Both offered alternatives fulfil REF-BM-08 (selecting item navigates to original url); a functionally-equivalent UI choice, not an opportunity. New-tab behaviour is orthogonal.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker offers Version A (type + Enter) vs Version B (select frequent tag). R7 client: 'I'd combine them: let me start typing, and as I do, show me any of my existing tags that match so I can just click one — and if it's new, Enter adds it.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Neither offered alternative realises REF-BM-10 (offer existing tags as autocomplete on entry): A is pure typing, B is pick-from-list without type-matching. Client supplies the reference-conforming autocomplete-on-type behaviour that neither option provided.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker: combined flow, type 'hea' -> select 'Health', type 'Walking' + Enter; 'matching ignores capitalisation and selecting preserves established spelling'. R8 client: 'Typing "hea" brought up my existing Health tag even though I used lowercase... ended up with both attached.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Revised presentation implementing the R7 correction; conforms to REF-BM-09 (assign multiple tags) and REF-BM-10 (case-insensitive autocomplete of existing tags).

decisions.evidence: R9 maker: filter by 'Health', 'one tag at a time, with All restoring the full library'; A buttons vs B dropdown. R9 client: 'filtering to one tag at a time with "All" bringing everything back is exactly how I'd expect'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Both alternatives fulfil REF-BM-11 (select a tag to filter); UI choice is functionally equivalent. Conforms to reference.

decisions.evidence: R10 maker: 'searches match partial words without caring about capitalisation, across titles, descriptions, website addresses, and tags'. R10 client: 'searching across the title, description, web address, and tags, matching partial words regardless of capitalisation, is just what I want'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Conforms to REF-BM-12 (full-text over title/description/url; note excluded because notes feature deferred) and REF-BM-13 (case-insensitive). Advanced operators/#tag/phrase (REF-BM-14/15/16) were never presented and are non-elicitation, not a divergence of the presented decision.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker: control stays on card, confirms immediately, selectable again to remove from Read Later; A icon vs B labelled. R11 client: 'stay on the card, confirm right away, and let me tap it again to take something back off my read-later list is just what I want'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Both alternatives fulfil REF-BM-17 (mark unread/read-later) and REF-BM-19 (mark read to remove); UI choice equivalent. Conforms.

decisions.evidence: R12 maker: dedicated Read-later view / toggle, shows count, switching back restores library. R12 client: 'switching between "All" and "Read later" as distinct views feels the most natural... seeing how many are waiting'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Both alternatives fulfil REF-BM-18 (view only unread separately). Conforms.

decisions.evidence: R13 maker summary of 'the settled experience now covers' lists eight flows with no editing or removal. R13 client: 'One thing I haven't seen yet that I'd expect as part of "managing"... once something's saved, I'd want to be able to tidy it up — fix a title or tags, or remove a link I no longer want.'
decisions.note: Specification/summary gate. The settled-so-far scope presented by the maker omitted editing (REF-BM-04) and deletion (REF-BM-05), both core items; client surfaces the gap and requests them (extend). Distinct from the later field-scope correction at R14.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker: 'I've currently limited post-save editing to the title and tags, leaving the website address and description unchanged... is that editing scope right?' R14 client: 'that's a bit narrower than I'd want... open editing up to at least the description as well... correct the web address too'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented editing scope (title+tags only) falls short of REF-BM-04 (edit url/title/description/tags). Client extends to include description and url editing — a separable aspect from the R13 existence capture.

decisions.evidence: R15 maker: revised flow edits description and web address plus title/tags; 'changing the web address does not automatically replace your edited title, description, or tags'. R15 client: 'I can now fix the description and correct the web address as well as the title and tags... This editing behavior matches my intent.'
decisions.note: Implementation/prototype review. Revised presentation implementing the R14 correction; conforms to REF-BM-04 full edit scope.

decisions.evidence: R16 maker: removal takes bookmark out of library and Read Later, other bookmarks/tags unaffected; A confirm vs B undo. R16 client: 'a removed bookmark leave both the library and Read Later while everything else and its tags stay untouched is exactly what I'd expect'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Both safety alternatives fulfil REF-BM-05 (delete); UI choice equivalent. Conforms (delete is permanent; archive/reversible distinction is deferred, see REF-BM-26/27/28 decision).

decisions.evidence: R19 maker offers Version A (tells you it already exists, takes you to the existing one) vs Version B (adds 'Save another copy'). R19 client: 'I prefer Version A... take me to the existing one... Being able to make a second copy on purpose, like in Version B, isn't something I want; that's exactly the clutter I'm trying to get away from.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Offered alternatives differ in fulfilment of REF-BM-06: A guides to the existing bookmark (conforming), B permits a duplicate (divergent). Client selects the conforming alternative and explicitly rejects the duplicate copy; trailing-slash normalisation also confirmed.

decisions.evidence: R26 maker: 'newest-first means when it was originally saved' and editing does not reorder. R26 client: 'I agree editing a bookmark shouldn't bump it to the top — newest-first should mean when I first saved it'. Client accepts the fixed ordering without requesting other sort keys.
decisions.note: Specification gate. REF-BM-22 requires sorting by a selectable sort key (date added, title, etc.); the presented ordering decision fixes a single newest-first order with no user-selectable sort. Divergence established from the presented ordering behaviour; passed without the client expressing the difference.

decisions.evidence: R7/R5 cards expose title, description, tags and website; R22 maker: compact readable cards, hidden text/tags 'remain fully searchable and editable'. R22 client: 'keeping long entries compact by default keeps my list tidy and easy to scan'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Readability-first list exposing title/description/tags per item conforms to REF-BM-07; the favicon aspect of REF-BM-07 is tracked under the REF-BM-02 favicon/preview divergence and is not double-counted here.

decisions.evidence: R1 client raises 'keeping my own notes on a bookmark' as a nice-to-have. R2 maker defers it; R2 client: 'personal notes... can come later.' Reaffirmed R27/R28: 'keeping my own notes on a bookmark... I'm happy to leave those for a future round, not this build.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Markdown notes (REF-BM-23) is a reference (extended) item omitted from the delivered scope. Client explicitly names the expectation and accepts the departure to a future cycle — an expressed requirement without implementation.

decisions.evidence: R1 client: 'tidying old ones out of the way without deleting them'. R2 client accepts 'putting old bookmarks out of sight... can come later'. Reaffirmed R28: 'hiding old bookmarks... I'd still like down the road... not part of this build'.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Archiving — hide-without-delete and its reversible-vs-permanent distinction and separate archived list (REF-BM-26/27/28) — omitted from delivered scope. Client explicitly identifies the expectation ('out of sight without deleting') and accepts deferral.

decisions.evidence: R1 client: 'being able to bring in the bookmarks I already have saved elsewhere'. R2 client: 'importing what I already have can come later'. Reaffirmed R28: 'importing I'd still like down the road... not part of this build'.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Import of existing bookmarks (REF-BM-30) omitted from delivered scope. Client explicitly states the expectation and accepts the departure. Export (REF-BM-31) was never raised and is treated as non-elicitation, not a decision.
